Introduction

This document will cover the usage of the ICE Data Services eSignal JStandard API – a Java version of ICE Data Services Standard API.

The eSignal JStandard API interfaces are written in Java. The API is being designed in such a way so that multiple ICE Data Services's low level APIs can be used with the same Java interfaces. For example, the API will provide one of the implementations using native (low-level) DBCAPI. Due to a very large scope of DBCAPI complete implementation, initially the API will target most of the functionalities as per client needs.

Library Components

eSignal JStandard API

This API will be used by the client to write their application. The API contains high level interfaces and an implementation that uses Native API to retrieve data from ICE Data Services servers.

List of files: (Archive Location: /dist)

  • ICEesig-jstandard-api-<version>.jar

Native API

This C/C++ API (DBCAPI) contains implementation for faster delivery of the content from ICE Data Services servers.

List of files: (Archive Location: /bin)

  • Windows-64 bit
    • dbcapi_64-<version>.dll (windows only)
    • PortLib_64-<version>.dll (windows only)
    • MD5Lib_64-<version>.dll (windows only)
  • Linux-64 bit
    • libdbcapi-<version>.so (linux only)
    • libport-<version>.so.0 (linux only)
    • libmd5_<version>.so.0 (linux only)
    • libpkware<version>.so (linux only)
    • libthreadallocv2<version>.so.0 (linux only)

Note: We are upgrading our library naming conventions to include version number and 64 versions. So you may see a name libdbcapi64-<version>.so

JNA Bridge

This API maps the Native methods to Java methods and makes it available to JStandard API for usage. It uses Sun's JNA technology in order to map to Java methods.

List of files: (Archive Location: /dist)

  • ICEesig-jstandard-dbcjna-<version>.jar

External API/Lib

These Libraries has to be installed on operating system. And the Java libraries should be available on the classpath since they are used by JStandard API. It is recommended to utilize the jar files provided as part of the versioned archive.

List of files: (Archive Location: /lib)

  • Windows
    • Redistributable - Visual C++ runtime to be installed on windows, available for download here and here (ATL security update). This API was last tested with "Microsoft Visual C++ 2005 Redistributable 8.0.59193".
  • Linux
    • librt.so on linux – Generally available: /lib64/librt<version>.so (linux)
  • Java (both Windows & Linux)
    • jna-<version>.jar
    • apache-commons-lang-<version>.jar
    • apache-commons-logging-<version>.jar
    • apache-commons-collections-<version>.jar
    • apache-commons-configuration-<version>.jar

Javadocs

The detail of the API interfaces, methods, & classes is available in the javadocs directory.

Application Setup

To start writing an application using JStandard API is no different theSignal JStandardany other Java library for the most part. The major difference here is dependency on Native Libraries. For your convenience we have created a property named "jna.library.path" in jstandard.properties which should point to the native library location.

  • Create your own Java application or open an existing one
  • Extract the archive ICEesig-jstandard-api-<version>.(tar|zip)
  • Add all the *.jar files provided under "bin" and "lib" directories to the classpath.
  • Create jstandard.properties and should be available at the root of application classpath.
    #windows *.dll location
    jna.library.path=C:\\ICEesig-jstandard-api\\bin
    #linux *.so location
    jna.library.path=/home/client/application/bin
    jstandard.DBC.program=`JTEST
    • Copy libdbcapi-<version>.so or *.dll to one of the application directory from "bin" directory.
    • Create a property inside jstandard.properties with name "jna.library.path" and path value which points to the directory in which dbcapi-<version>.so/*.dll resides.
    • Copy libport-<version>.so/*.dll ( e.g. from "/samples/bin" directory) to user/application libraries directory, so that it's available to the library linker.
    • Override a default property "jstandard.DBC.program" with your application name, the default value is "`JTEST" (The name cannot have more than 13 characters).
  • Linux only:
    • Login as a root to the Linux machine.
    • Copy command: cp <extracted-api-dir>/bin/lib*-<version>.so /usr/lib64/.
    • Copy command: cp <extracted-api-dir>/bin/lib*-<version>.so.0 /usr/lib64/.
    • All the binaries except libdbcapi should be copied to allow native access to the library.
    • Give execute permission to lib*-<version>.so command: chmod 755 /usr/lib64/libport-<version>.so.0
    • Make sure librt-<version>.so is also available as part of system libraries. Generally included as part of Linux installation. (/lib64 directory)

Linux Note: libdbcapi-<version>.so always links to the "libport", "libmd5", "librt", etc. and other default C libraries. (Use "ldd libdbcapi-<version>.so" command to find out all the libraries dependencies) The JNA bridge uses the library linker to find out the native libraries that it depends upon. And it looks at the default system and user libraries directory in order to resolve the dependencies.

Windows Note: dbcapi-<version>.dll also links to "PortLib", "MD5Lib", Visual studio runtime libraries etc. You might want to use a program called dependency walker (google it) if you are receiving "jna.library.path" exception. Again the JNA bridge uses the library linker to find out native libraries that it depends upon.

Logging Setup

  1. The API uses open source standard apache commons logging which supports all major Java log implementations. For example, add log4j-<version>.jar and log4j.properties in the root of the application.
  2. We have added native logger control starting build esignal-jstandard-01-001-0006. The logger name is "CPLUSPLUS" depending on the logger implementation that you use. Here is an example of log4j entry. Version esignal-jstandard-01-001-0006 support ERROR, INFO and DEBUG levels.
log4j.logger.CPLUSPLUS=INFO, console, dailylog

Sample

A sample is also provided with the most basic client application. The application shows the usage of JStandard API. Please read the documents provided under Sample's "/docs" directory for full details on working of the sample.

Support

The ICE Data Services eSignal JStandard API has been written on top of the ICE Data Services's popular DBCAPI. For any support questions, please email to Developer@theice.com

FAQs

  • Why program is receiving code "DbcOpenConnection failed with code: -111" error?
    • Please contact our support group to receive appropriate DBC program name.
  • Why program is receiving "jna.library.path points to the right directory" exception?
    • A: Use External API/Lib tab on the user's guide for example, if you are running on Windows, make sure you have downloaded Microsoft Redistributable.
  • Why program is receiving "NotSupportedException" or "ResourceManagerException with implementation is not available"?
    • A: DBC or LIGHTWEIGHT are always partial implementation depending on the server capabilities. To keep things consistent across different implementation an interface was created to serve the market data information.
